issue: PMAT-520 (closes forjar#520) — the forjar 1.29.0 release cut: the version and lockfile bumped together, the twelve behaviour bullets written under CHANGELOG [1.29.0] for the first time (the section was EMPTY with twelve tickets merged behind it), docs/audits/crux-1.29.0.md reconciling every one of them against 28 surveyed systems, and the dogfood receipt recording `make dogfood-release` exit 0 with all nine gates green and coverage at 96.43%. Twelve PRs across fifteen tickets since v1.28.0, every one labelled release:v1.29.0 at the moment it merged. Three review lanes read the record looking for a sentence a reader could check and find false; they found four, and all four are corrected here.
recorded_at: after the round, the four corrections, and the two refutations that do not reproduce

quorum.rounds: one crux survey lane over the ten bullets that existed when it ran, and one round of three sandboxed review lanes on 3875e2de with --not-before pinned to the dispatch instant. All three returned, exits 0/0/0, durations 367s/478s/389s, verdicts 3/3 FAIL.
quorum.kill_rule: six numbered claims, and ABOVE them one standing instruction: find a sentence in the CHANGELOG, the crux audit or the dogfood receipt that a reader could check and find false. FOUR of the five findings came from that instruction rather than from the claims. A release record is prose, and prose fails in a way a claim list does not anticipate — not by being unsupported, but by drifting a word or a count away from what the tree says. None of the four would have failed a gate; all four would have been in the permanent record of what 1.29.0 was.
refuted_claims: That thirteen PRs across sixteen tickets merged into this release — twelve and fifteen. Gate A enumerates the window; the thirteenth is this cut's own PR, which has not merged. Refuted 3/3.

That nothing a cut needs is missing — README.md:96 read `forjar = "1.28"` while the tree builds 1.29.0. Gate D passed it and is CORRECT by its predicate (a caret admits 1.29.0), but its own comment names a README that has fallen behind as the defect and the code only fails on a claim that is NEWER. Corrected by hand; the gate's gap is PMAT-526 (#526), filed rather than widened inside a release cut.
That crux row 1 describes what gate T does — it said forjar 'refuses the tag'; gate T refuses the ledger ROW, and the tag exists by then, which is why a release is three PRs.

That the release changes no source file — twelve .rs files differ from v1.28.0 and zero are under src/. Gate F's own line was precise about the BRANCH; the prose generalised it into a false claim about the release.

That the CB-21xx figures in the CHANGELOG read as what they are — two lanes read finding counts as a list of ceilings. A writing defect rather than a false statement, and a number three readers misread is a defect even when it is true.
lane_errors: One lane called the roster arithmetic impossible — '172 - 6 + 1 = 167, not 166'. Measured: 172 - 6 = 166 exactly, because CB-148 is in BOTH rosters, printed as 'RETIRED — superseded by CB-2110' in the first. Does not reproduce.

All three reported the dogfood receipt as having no falsification block. It does not, because a dogfood receipt does not carry one — its shape is fixed by the forjar-dogfood skill. The brief said the receipt 'will name' the reverted hunk without saying which receipt. A BRIEF defect, recorded as one.
The delegate stopped at its 30-turn limit while summarising, after all three lanes completed and reduce.json was written. Fifth occurrence in this session at exactly that point.

The first receipt for this cut pointed its falsification at a PRE-EXISTING green test, falsification_crux_gate_reads_the_release_section, and the quorum gate refused it by name: a falsification must exercise the change under review. It was right, and the answer was not a different pointer but a gate — T9 exists because three lanes caught by hand what no gate asked.

falsification.test: T9, the gate arm this cut's own defect called for: while a cut is in flight, any "<N> PRs across <M> tickets" claim in the release's own CHANGELOG section must equal what the window measures. a_changelog_that_counts_its_own_pr_is_named_and_red drives the exact defect; the_measured_count_passes_in_either_case drives the true count in both capitalisations and the singular; a_section_that_makes_no_claim_is_not_failed_for_silence keeps a prose convention from becoming an obligation; a_neighbouring_release_section_is_not_this_ones_claim refuses reading the wrong section, which would be GREEN on an incorrect cut whose predecessor happened to match; between_releases_a_stale_count_is_not_this_gates_business keeps it off the tree when nothing is being cut
falsification.reverted: the CHANGELOG exactly as it was written at 3875e2de, committed in a `git clone --shared` throwaway because gate T reads the CHANGELOG at HEAD; and separately docs/audits/crux-1.29.0.md removed from the working tree, which turns gate H red
falsification.observed_failure: GATE T FAIL CHANGELOG [1.29.0] claims "Thirteen PRs across sixteen tickets" and the window measures "Twelve PRs across Fifteen tickets": 12 PR(s) merged since v1.28.0 carrying 15 ticket(s). A cut's own PR has not merged when the sentence is written, and counting it is the error this arm exists for. GATE T PASS at 80c2ffbf with the count corrected. And GATE H FAIL no docs/audits/crux-1.29.0.md: 12 behaviour(s) are being released against no recorded comparison, green with it restored. Both in docs/audits/logs/PMAT-520-cut.log. THE RED HALF RAN IN A SCRATCH CLONE: gate T reads the CHANGELOG at HEAD, so the proof needs the defect COMMITTED, and committing-then-resetting inside a proof script has destroyed work twice in this session — the second time it took the T9 commit itself, recovered from the reflog.
falsification.still_green_when_reverted: the nineteen cases of falsification_release_goals_are_measured and the eight of falsification_release_cookbook_is_part_of_the_release, which drive every other arm of gate T through the same fixture and prove T9 is confined to the in-flight window

crux.verdict: accept(twelve rows against 28 surveyed systems and 36 [X] claims, in docs/audits/crux-1.29.0.md. FOUR rows conclude forjar is WORSE than the industry default and they are the four worth reading first: clearing shared /tmp by hand where systemd, Docker and Podman have isolation; a release gate whose telemetry depends on shell pipelines, with eighteen SIGPIPE sites open as PMAT-240; a dated ceiling that records debt without naming the release at which it stops being tolerated, which is what Bazel's --incompatible_* flags do; and a cycle refused at run time where Bazel, Nix and systemd refuse one at declaration time. Two review lanes independently identified the same four and neither found a row claiming a win it had not earned. Rows 11 and 12 are the orchestrator's rather than the survey lane's, because neither behaviour existed when the lane ran, and the audit says so in its own limit section.)
